ACQUIRING REUSABLE SPECTRAL COMPUTATION AND ITS TRACE WEIGHTS
Astra learning/computation branch — 31 October 2026

STATUS

This is an ordinary constructive research note. The main exact-arithmetic
construction has received complementary mathematical reviews. A finite-grid
extension, a centre-only reconstruction, and a cumulative admission construction
are given separately so their interfaces and costs remain visible. Exact rational
and floating-point programs accompany the note. Floating-point experiments do
not certify exact rank, robustness, novelty, or a practical speed advantage.

The central candidate contribution is the combined acquisition theorem:
unknown matrix-algebra acquisition, exact recovery of exhausted multiplicities,
tracial averaging of the remaining multiplicities, and one confidence event for
the entire positive cone of all future expressions. The algebraic ingredients,
Krylov closure, symmetry reduction, and inverse-epsilon single-trace estimation
are established mathematics. Historical novelty of this complete combination
and superiority over a strong retaining algebra learner remain unestablished.

1. SCIENTIFIC QUESTION AND CAPABILITY

Can a computational system acquire operations that support many later, previously
unspecified numerical calculations, instead of relearning each answer? The target
chosen here is a reusable spectral and trace service for a fixed family of large,
possibly dense, full-rank, noncommuting operators. Later questions can contain
new coefficients, sums, products, adjoints, inverses where defined, spectral
functions, and positive matrix pencils. They may be chosen after seeing the
acquired representation and its random probes.

This is a numerical computation interface: a submitted vector v returns A_j v.
It is stronger than passive observations or the scalar-return experimental
interface in Astra N1515/N1521. No physical mechanism for implementing arbitrary
vector queries is inferred from those sources. Every comparator receives the
same vector interface, and every original action is charged.

The valuable regime is small generated algebra rather than small matrix rank.
For example, A_j=U [direct_sum_alpha (B_j,alpha tensor I_malpha)] U*, with hidden
dense U and small noncommuting blocks B_j,alpha, can have rank N for every j.
Ordinary low-rank output-range compression does not explain its tractability.

# Independent audit of the hybrid exact/estimated multiplicity theorem

## Audit conclusion

The proposed theorem is valid in the exact matrix-vector / exact-rank / exact-decomposition model. I found no dependency error from learning the central projectors using the same random seeds. Its correctness follows from three facts: joint cyclic multiplicity is min(m,q r), unsaturated multiplicities are exact, and unresolved blocks necessarily have enough Gaussian degrees of freedom for a 1/epsilon seed bound.

The significant remaining qualifications are acquisition/decomposition cost, numerical rank visibility, and comparison with existing matrix-* algebra reduction and Hutch++-type rank-aware trace estimation. This audit does not establish historical novelty or an advantage over the strongest retaining implementation.

## Complete statement

Let a fixed unital complex matrix *-algebra A, generated by k fixed Hermitian N-by-N matrices, act as

    A ≅ direct_sum_(alpha=1)^b (M_(r_alpha)(C) tensor I_(m_alpha)).

Let d=sum r_alpha^2. Draw q independent standard complex Gaussian vectors g_1,...,g_q in C^N, with E|g_(j,l)|^2=1. Acquire

    K_q = sum_(j=1)^q A g_j.

Let its exact compressed algebra be decomposed into inequivalent simple factors, with irrep dimension r_alpha and represented multiplicity s_alpha. Almost surely,

    s_alpha = min(m_alpha, q r_alpha),
    D_q = dim K_q = sum r_alpha s_alpha <= min(N,q d).

The compressed algebra is faithful almost surely.

Define a block as resolved if s_alpha<q r_alpha, and unresolved otherwise. For a resolved block set mhat_alpha=s_alpha. For an unresolved block set

    w_alpha = sum_(j=1)^q ||P_alpha g_j||^2,
    mhat_alpha = w_alpha/(q r_alpha),

where P_alpha is the canonical ambient isotypic central projector. Its restriction is learned by the compressed decomposition, so w_alpha is computable from the seed coordinates in K_q.

For X=direct_sum (X_alpha tensor I_(m_alpha)) in A, define

    T_hat(X) = sum_alpha mhat_alpha tr(X_alpha).

For 0<epsilon<1, 0<delta<1, choose

    q >= ceil( 2 sqrt(log(2b/delta)) / epsilon ).

Then, with probability at least 1-delta, simultaneously for every PSD X in A,

    (1-epsilon) Tr(X) <= T_hat(X) <= (1+epsilon) Tr(X).

The event is uniform, so X may be selected adaptively using every seed, all learned coordinates, previous estimates, and arbitrarily many earlier computations. T

# Final focused review of MAIN_PROOF.txt

Reviewed the combined source and cumulative_exact.py / cumulative_exact_results.json. Scope: theorem constants, centre separation, confidence inversion, costs, and the separate cumulative construction. This is a focused internal mathematical review, not historical novelty certification.

## Accepted items

* The moment-curve centre search is valid: at most binom(b,2)(b-1) integer choices can collide, so the stated number of trials suffices. Minimal-polynomial degree b certifies separation.
* The corrected complex-Gaussian bound uses epsilon^2/4; the stated q and the separately stated real-Gaussian constants are sound.
* The centre-only dimensions and one-copy trace formulas are correct, using the full compressed algebra basis.
* The Gamma deviance tail bound is correct. Its interval inversion needs the boundary convention below.
* Source actions, full-vector handling, algebra/centre work, exact bit costs, and downstream evaluation remain distinguished. The result does not claim free word execution or unrestricted optimization.
* Same-seed central-projector dependence and finite-grid rank/concentration union bounds are appropriately qualified.
* The cumulative relation construction maintains injective witnesses and charges residual-word execution. Its fixture reports 24 product candidates, 188 acquisition source actions, and 48 separate truth-check actions. These counts match the code and the stated restricted purpose.

## Three scoped corrections — incorporated and checked

Final consistency check confirmed all three patches below are incorporated in MAIN_PROOF.txt. Section 2 also explicitly distinguishes ideal exact-root operations for general complex sources from the finite-bit rational-source algorithm.
